item.title: Black Friday has made smart video doorbells ridiculously cheap — here are 5 deals starting at $22
item.dc:content:
Best Black Friday Deals: at your service!
On the hunt for big Black Friday 2026 savings on this type of gear? Our team of experts has been tracking the best offers from the sales event so far — click through to find out more.

Smart video doorbells used to be quite expensive, but unlike smartphones, which have gotten considerably more expensive over the past year, video doorbells seem to have gone in the opposite direction. You can get a pretty good one for surprisingly little money these days, with even some of the cheaper models offering features like 2K video recording, night vision, and two-way audio.

And thanks to the ongoing Black Friday sale, they've gotten even cheaper. In fact, some of the biggest names in the smart home space, including Ring, Arlo, and Blink, are offering discounts of over 50% on their video doorbells right now. I've rounded up five deals worth checking out, including a couple of options that don't require a monthly subscription to save your recordings.

What's even better is that four of them cost less than $40/

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Best Black Friday video doorbell deals

Wired Doorbell 2K+: was $49.99 now $21.99
If you're looking for an affordable way to get started with smart home security, it's hard to argue with this $22 Blink video doorbell. It offers 2K video quality with a head-to-toe view, night vision, and noise cancellation for clearer conversations. Since it's a wired doorbell, you don't have to worry about recharging it either. You'll need a compatible Alexa device or a separately sold Blink Chime for in-home doorbell alerts, though.View Deal

Wireless Video Doorbell 2K (2nd Gen): was $79.99 now $28.02
If you'd rather get a wireless video doorbell, Arlo's second-generation model is available for just $28. It offers 2K HDR video, two-way audio, and night vision, so you can see and speak to whoever's at your front door even at night. There's also support for person and package detection, though you'll need an Arlo Secure subscription to access those advanced features.View Deal

D205 2K Wireless Video Doorbell: was $49.99 now $37.98
At just $38, the Tapo D205 is a great option if you don't want to pay for a subscription or a separate storage hub. It supports local recording via a microSD card of up to 512GB and offers AI-powered person detection at no extra cost. You also get a 2K camera with a 160-degree field of view, night vision, two-way audio, and a built-in 5,200 mAh battery for up to 180 days of use.View Deal

Battery Doorbell 2K (2nd Gen): was $99.99 now $38.99
If you already have a couple of Amazon Echo devices around your house, this Ring video doorbell is probably the one I'd recommend. It features video with up to 6x zoom, two-way audio, and motion alerts. You can also receive doorbell notifications through your Echo speakers or pull up the live camera feed on an Echo Show.View Deal

Security Video Doorbell E340: was $169.99 now $89.99
The Eufy E340 is a little more expensive than the other video doorbells on this list, but it comes with two cameras: one to see who's at your front door and another to keep an eye on your packages. You also get 2K video and 8GB of built-in local storage without a monthly subscription. Plus, you can use it as either a wired or battery-powered doorbell. View Deal

Personally, I'd spend a little extra on a video doorbell that supports local storage. It's nice being able to go back and check what happened outside your house without having to pay for yet another monthly subscription.

The Tapo D205 is particularly appealing in that regard at just $38. That said, if you regularly get packages delivered to your doorstep, the dual-camera setup on the Eufy E340 might be worth the extra money.

item.title: These super portable and stylish Beats earbuds are just £39 with free delivery right now
item.dc:content:
When I'm in a rush to leave the house, there's only one pair of earbuds that I shove into my pocket without a second thought: the Beats Solo Buds.

They're extremely compact and lightweight thanks to a sophisticated design that ditches the usual clunky earpod case battery and instead crams 18 hours of juice into each bud on a single charge, so they're easy to take on the go.

Better still, their Fast Fuel quick-charging feature means that you can squeeze an hour of playback out of a single hour of charge – and this is something I rely on all the time. I plug the buds directly into my phone's charging port when they're dead for a quick charge when I need a bit of extra juice. It's a real lifesaver and means that, as long as I carry a small cable, I never have to worry about being without my tunes.

At just £39 (was £79), thanks to a mega EE discount, they're also simply incredible value and pack in plenty of that trademark Beats sound despite the small form factor. Beats may be owned by Apple, but that doesn't mean the Solo Buds don't play nice with Android. They support Google Fast Pair, and even have an Android companion app. (If you are an Apple user, they work perfectly with that ecosystem, too.)

  • Browse the full EE Black Friday sale

Solo Buds: was £79 now £39
These compact earbuds are a steal at under £40. They come in a wide range of attractive colors (though the translucent red is my personal favorite) and are both practical and stylish. EE is even throwing in free delivery.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You're after a seriously compact pair of earbuds that you won't need to worry about keeping charged.

The Beats Solo Buds are some of the smallest and lightest wireless earbuds I've ever used when in their case, making them easy to take on the go. The Fast Fuel feature also makes them very quick to top up with charge, even when you're out and about.

❌Skip this deal if: You want to spend more and get better sound. Although I think the Beats Solo Buds can hold their own in the under £100 audio space with their poppy and bassy sound, the brand doesn't exactly have a reputation for audiophile quality.

If you want to spend more on something that sounds even better, you have plenty of options to choose from in the ongoing sales.

item.title: This Android AirTag alternative is now less than $7 a pop — they're rechargeable, with louder alarms
item.dc:content:
If you're like me, you put your keys down the second you get into the house and immediately forget where you left them.

That's where smart tags come in: these little trackers tell you exactly where you've put whatever one is attached to and will guide you straight to its location. They can even emit an alarm sound, making it easier to find something that you might have stowed away in a pocket or desk drawer.

Apple's AirTag is a popular choice, but right now mobile accessory maker Ugreen is selling a four-pack of its Android alternative for just $26.99 (down from $33.99) at Amazon as part of its Black Friday sales. That's right, a pack of not one or two but (count 'em) four standalone smart tags that you can attach to your keys, stow in your luggage, and so on. That works out to just under $7 per tag!

The Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags are fully compatible with Google's Find Hub, so you don't need to worry about Android compatibility. Despite being cheaper, they also boast some advantages compared to other trackers. Namely, batteries that you can recharge via USB Type-C and a louder speaker to make them even easier to locate when you need to use the alarm.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack: was $33.99 now $26.99
These little smart tags are perfect if you keep losing your keys or otherwise want to keep track of your stuff. They're rechargeable via USB-C and fully compatible with Google's Find Hub.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You want affordable smart trackers that work well with an Android phone to keep track of your keys or other small objects.

❌Skip this deal if: You don't think the trackers will be useful, or you don't need four. If you can't think of anything that you would be likely to lose, then chances are these trackers are not a good investment.

Similarly, if you would rather spend the same amount or more on just a single tracker, then there are other options available.

item.title: Perfect for teens: Motorola is currently selling a smartphone for under $100, so you don't have to worry about paying a fortune for a replacement if they break it
item.dc:content:
There's nothing more frustrating than buying a family member a shiny new gadget only to find out they've broken it within just a couple of weeks. If you're using the ongoing Black Friday sales to pick up a handset for someone a little clumsier than most, whether that's a teen or someone much older, then there's no reason to break the bank splashing out on something they might, well, break.

That's why this entry-level smartphone from Motorola has my attention. The Moto G Play is on sale for just $99.99 at Amazon right now, a $50 price cut compared to its usual asking price. That's right, you can get a fully fledged smartphone from a big name brand for under 100 bucks right now, and it's even unlocked so it can be used with every carrier.

What exactly do you get for that money? A basic, all-round phone geared towards day-to-day use cases like making calls and browsing social media or the web. No, it's nothing fancy, but I'd argue this actually works in its favor: this is a phone for keeping in touch rather than playing games all day.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Moto G Play (2024): was $149.99 now $99.99
This dirt-cheap smartphone is geared towards those with basic needs who just want something that enables them to keep in touch. Its specs are very basic, and the construction is plastic, but it still makes calls, can browse the web, and download apps all the same.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You want one of the cheapest phones available from a major brand. The Moto G Play is one of the cheapest phones that you can get, especially when it's discounted to under $100 like this, which is reflected by the specs and build. It does have some highlights, though, like the 90Hz refresh rate of its screen for a smoother feel and the presence of a 3.5mm headphone jack and microSD card slot.

❌Skip this deal if: You're after more than the bare minimum. The Moto G Play is a cheap phone for a reason: it has low-end specs and a decidedly budget feel compared to more premium options.

If you want to spend more on something that's more capable, then you can find better options in my list of the best budget Android phone deals right now.

item.title: The Fitbit Charge 6 is less than $125 this Black Friday, and it’s ideal if you’re serious about getting fit in the new year
item.dc:content:
Black Friday gives you an extra chance to get as many holiday gifts as you can at discounted prices or, if you're already thinking about the new year, it's the perfect time to accumulate devices to start 2027 with a bang. Of course, I'm talking about the best fitness trackers.

Best Black Friday Deals:
On the hunt for big Black Friday 2026 savings on this type of gear? Our team of experts has been tracking the best offers from the sales event so far — click through to find out more.View Deal

Out of all the wearables we've tested, the Fitbit Charge 6 has been the sovereign of our list of top health monitoring devices, and it's been that way for the past three years. Now it's cheaper than before, dropping down to $122 from $159.95 in Amazon's monster Black Friday sale.

Kick-starting your new year's fitness goals is better said than done, but believe me, once you have a good smartwatch or fitness tracker cuffed to your wrist, it helps you build a better understanding of your health patterns, helping you build a better relationship with your body. This makes the journey even more enjoyable.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

The Fitbit Charge 6 hasn't budged from the top spot in our best fitness trackers list since its release three years ago, which shows how it's stood the test of time. It's not the biggest saving, and certainly not a record-low price, but its health-monitoring tools make it worth the spend. It was slightly cheaper during last year's Black Friday event, so it wouldn't hurt to keep your eyes open for another possible price drop. View Deal

✅Recommended if: Your current Fitbit doesn't pack Google's slew of health tracking tools, and you want the upgrade. Due to its small bezel, it's a wonder to wear while you sleep, which I've found frustrating with wearables — particularly smartwatches.

If you prefer smaller wearables that aren't too obtrusive, but still pack the punch with smarts, the Fitbit Charge 6 does just that. With three GPS settings, AFib detection, heart rate variability, breathing rate, and blood oxygen tracking, its small build packs quite the roster of features.

❌Skip this deal if: You want a fitness tracker with a larger, brighter screen. The Fitbit Charge 6 has all the smarts you need for a wearable, but in comparison to other models, its screen isn't the easiest to navigate. The Fitbit Charge 6 works to its full potential with a Google Health Premium subscription too, which is another setback if you don't want to pay for more than the device itself.

However, the only features you'll miss out on if you go subscription-free are Daily Readiness and guided workout programs, which not everyone needs. Other than that, it does pretty much everything else you need, so a subscription isn't a big requirement.

item.dc:content:
The countdown to Black Friday has officially begun, and with less than 24 hours to go, we're really starting to feel the adrenaline. And as a team of phone-obsessives, our eyes have lit up at the sight of the live Android phone deals.

The Best Amazon Echo Black Friday Deals

Black Friday Android deals started a few days ago, but if you've been patient and suppressed your impulse-buying urges to find better discounts, we salute you. It was probably for the best too, because prices for flagship models across Samsung, Google, and more have dropped even more.

Out of all the Black Friday deals we've found, it's clear that the Samsung Galaxy S26 series is the star of the show, with price drops across both its mid-range and premium models. At the same time, Google has also pulled through with record-low deals on the Pixel 11 line-up that will be gone by the end of the weekend.

That said, we're still a few hours away from Black Friday itself, so these deals could literally go in any direction. If it were to go our way, we'd like to see one more small price drop to steer us into the weekend — but one can only dream.

View Deal

View Deal

Though it's a small upgrade from its predecessor, it still makes a great device if you're after a trendy phone that's light and thin, with powerful software running through its veins. View Deal

Pixel 10 (128GB): was $799 now $593
For those of you who aren't too fussed with keeping up with the latest models, the Pixel 10 packs similar AI features to the Pixel 11 (albeit not to the same level), but that shouldn't put you off — especially not at this price tag. Its support for Qi2 allows you to take advantage of wireless charging, and its improved battery can take you through the entire day on a single charge. View Deal

item.title: These bumper Black Friday Chromebook deals prove that capable computing doesn't have to cost an arm and a leg
item.dc:content:
Chromebooks offer one of the most affordable and reliable avenues into computing. These budget-friendly laptops are powered by Google's ChromeOS, a lightweight operating system built around the Google Chrome browser. Unlike Windows, which can struggle massively on cheaper devices, ChromeOS is highly optimized and run smoothly even on low-end specs.

The Best Budget Black Friday Deals For Android Fans

This makes Chromebooks an excellent pick for those with more basic computing needs, or who just want a laptop that works well and doesn't cost a fortune. Although they are limited to browser-based apps, there are loads of advantages to a Chromebook too.

They boot quickly and are exceptionally secure: in fact, Google claims that no Chromebook has ever been infected with a virus. They also pair fantastically with an Android phone, with a level of cross-functionality that Google users will seriously appreciate.

Of course, the ongoing Black Friday sales represent the perfect chance to secure a capable Chromebook at a discount – so I've rounded up the best deals from the sale below along with some commentary on the key specs to help you make up your mind.

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Today's best deals — Chromebooks

Chromebook CX15: was $234.99 now $197
This dirt cheap ASUS model is limited in all the ways you would expect from an under $200 laptop: just 4GB of RAM and a modest processor. There are some big wins on the spec sheet though, like the 128GB of storage and FHD 15.6" panel which actually makes it better than some of the more expensive options on this list in a few regards.View Deal

Chromebook m 14": was $289.99 now $245.99
This 14" Lenovo Chromebook is limited by its 64GB of storage, but it does offer 8GB of RAM for smooth multitasking. The MediaTek Kompanio 540 chip isn't the fastest either, though it's more than enough for ChromeOS and the screen is just okay for the price. View Deal

Chromebook CX14: was $289.99 now $239.99
This 14-inch Chromebook has an Intel Celeron N4500 chip suitable for basic browsing needs, but the 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage could limit your ability to multi-task. The 1920 x 1080 resolution of the display is good for the price, though.View Deal

Chromebook CM15: was $325.99 now $249.99
This ASUS model has a better screen than the Lenovo Chromebook m 14", but it loses on RAM and offers the same processor and storage. The design is a bit more stylish too, which might make it a better pick if you're concerned about aesthetics.View Deal

Chromebook 2-in-1: was $509.99 now $329.99
Getting into more premium territory now. This 2-in-1 model functions as both a laptop and a tablet thanks to its folding design and 1920x1200 touch-screen display. The Intel N150 chip is also better performing than the lower-priced options, and you get 128GB of storage. The only caveat here is the 4GB of RAM, which might limit the number of tabs you can have open at once.

Chromebook Spin 314: was $499.99 now $339.99
Now this is a bargain, with the most powerful chipset so far and a well-considered spec sheet all-round. This Intel Core i3-N305 powered 2-in-1 convertible features a matte-texture touch screen, 8GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage plus a HD webcam for crisp video calls. It even comes with a free carrying case!View Deal

Chromebook m 15": was $462.91 now $349.99
If you want something a little larger than the usual 14-inch form factor, this 15-inch model could be a good pick. The MediaTek Kompanio 540 chip is suitable for most day-to-day tasks, and you get 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage which is plenty.View Deal

Chromebook Plus

Chromebook Plus 514: was $599.99 now $499.99
This Chromebook Plus model is the most premium on this entire list, and comes with some unique software features. The Intel Core i3-1315U chipset is fast and responsive, while the 8GB of RAM makes multi-tasking a breeze. There's also 256GB of storage, which is more than enough for the vast majority of users. That's on top of a 1920x1080 touchscreen display and even a backlit keyboard.View Deal

The Motorola Razr Plus 2025 is $500 at Amazon, a $100 (17%) discount off its regular $600 price. That's the lowest price we've seen for this foldable, making it one of the most tempting Black Friday phone deals to check out. The deal is for the Hot Pink model with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.

The appeal of the Razr Plus 2025 begins with its compact, pocket-friendly size. Closed, it is small enough to fit into tight pockets or small bags without the bulk of a traditional slab phone.

It's a great smartphone accessory to have on hand, especially when you're traveling, as using your phone for navigation, taking pictures, and staying connected throughout the day can drain even the biggest smartphone batteries pretty quickly.

Thankfully, some of the biggest charging accessory brands, including Anker, Baseus, and Ugreen, are offering pretty good discounts this Black Friday. item.title: One UI 9.5 could save your Galaxy S24, S25 from the 9.0 update's battery problems
item.dc:content:
Any big software update can come with its share of problems. For Samsung, those problems appeared in the form of battery drain. A recent update suggests a fix is in the works.

A user in Samsung's Turkish community reiterated problems they've experienced since downloading One UI 9 (via Android Authority). The user states battery health "dropped to abnormally low levels on many devices..." After the user raised the issue with Samsung, the company issued an official response, saying it is working on it.

Samsung has confirmed that the battery health issue many users have experienced in One UI 9 will be fixed with its One UI 9.5 upgrade. The user adds that this problem occurred "even on newer devices." The situation remains somewhat mysterious. Samsung says the issue "will be resolved." However, the problem raised—the issue users have reported—is about battery health.

The publication questioned this as well, wondering whether One UI 9 was misrepresenting devices' true battery health. If the opposite is true and batteries were truly damaged, that's an entirely different situation, as SamMobile mentioned. While it's good to see Samsung is at least working toward a solution, we're still far off.

One UI 9 wasn't flawless

One UI 9 was delayed (*exasperated sigh*), and its arrival on some older phones wasn't great. Once the patch hit Galaxy S24 phones, users quickly noticed severe battery drain. An S24 user stated that, under "heavy use," their device's battery plummeted ~94% in about five hours. While, yes, they were using their phone often, the drop was excessive. Another Galaxy S25 user reported that their phone, which sat idle most of the day, dropped 40%.

Regarding the battery health/degradation issue, the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 only started last week. According to the changelog, Samsung is giving testers a chance to experiment with App Lock (protect apps with biometrics), improved Pro camera controls, Mindful Note journaling, and more. Knowing how Samsung's beta programs go, it will be a while before anyone sees relief from the current software woes.

item.title: 1Password confirms backend data breach — here’s what hackers actually stole
item.dc:content:
1Password has confirmed that its internal systems have been compromised, exposing the personal information of a subset of customers.

In a blog post, the company admitted it had been breached after a hacker took over an employee's GitHub account, exposing customer names, email addresses and account recovery tokens. However, your actual passwords remain securely stored, per the disclosure. The company disclosed the intrusion on November 25, six days after first spotting the suspicious activity.

The attacker used the compromised corporate GitHub account to access private source code repositories and compromised 1Password’s CI/CD build system and pushed malicious code to backend services. That rogue code exfiltrated admin records for a subset of customers, including user IDs, last sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters and tokens from emailed invitation and recovery links.

1Password says your encrypted vaults, Secret Keys, master passwords and browser extensions were not accessed. Its architecture ensures that even its servers can't read your vault keys, so the hacker got nothing from the password perspective.

Stolen recovery tokens may sound scary, but they can't be used to unlock an account without single sign-on credentials or an emailed verification code. To stop brute-force guessing, 1Password extended those email codes from six digits to 10 alphanumeric characters.

1Password has disabled the hijacked GitHub account, rotated internal credentials, tightened endpoint controls and hired outside cybersecurity investigators since discovering the attack on November 19. Management says there’s no evidence of actual account takeovers and has directly notified users with exposed pending tokens, but it’s unclear if every affected customer was alerted.

At this time, you do not need to change your master password or Secret Key. But keep your phishing radar on high alert: The company warns that scammers now know your name, email and that you use 1Password, giving them prime tools for convincing fake recovery emails. It’s worth noting to never enter your credentials through an email link; rather, open the official 1Password app directly.

item.title: The market is suffering, and phone makers are reportedly cutting back drastically in 2027
item.dc:content:
A major report has surfaced this midweek, stating smartphone OEMs are making drastic changes in preparation for 2027. Companies are reportedly preparing to cut back on shipment estimates, and we can attribute it to only one thing.

Tipster Jukan on X highlighted a report by Jiemian (Chinese), saying smartphone makers are lowering their expected 2027 shipment totals. Major companies such as Samsung are reportedly lowering next year's shipments by almost 10%. That would reduce its totals to ~210 million units. Another eye-catching name is Apple. The publication claims Apple is cutting its phone shipments by 5.6% in 2027, bringing units to around ~233 million.

For Motorola, estimated shipments may drop by 20% to 40 million units. This comes as the Signature 27 debuts, pre-orders begin, and the phone starts to gain traction. What's more, rumors suggest an early foldable launch.

Other popular Android OEMs like Xiaomi are reportedly estimating a 25% reduction in shipments, while Vivo could cut back the most, by 29%, in 2027. Curiously, Google wasn't mentioned in this report, but that doesn't mean things will remain the same.

It's clear where this is coming from

We've already seen the beginnings of Samsung's cutback in October. The company reportedly asked suppliers to reduce smartphone production by 20% to 30% in Q4 2026. The reduction would bring Samsung's 2026 totals closer to 200 million units, down from the projected 270 million. On the other hand, a Counterpoint Research report echoes phone OEM woes.

In Q3, the smartphone market reached its lowest point in 14 years. The market plummeted by 20% YoY. Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain said, "The extreme memory shortage is pushing the smartphone market into a more selective phase." The phone market has suffered this badly since 2012, and we're all looking at how demanding AI has been.

As DRAM and NAND shortages push OEMs into a corner, prices are soaring. As prices soar, "consumer behavior" changes. Counterpoint's Jain added, "Consumers are holding on to their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices." Q2 wasn't as drastic, but it still marked a 4% decline in the market, according to Omdia's research.

item.title: Galaxy Z TriFold 2 rumors see it packaged with Samsung's next summer foldables
item.dc:content:
Foldables are sticking around—especially wide foldables. However, let's not forget about the ambitious "TriFold." Rumors suggest Samsung's working on a sequel for a couple of familiar markets.

Early this morning (Nov. 25), folks at GalaxyClub (Dutch) suggest Samsung is following old habits, citing the TriFold 2's alleged codename (via GSMArena). The post says the upcoming Galaxy Z9 series (specifically the Fold 9) has been marked with the codename Q9. However, it reportedly found another device codenamed "Q9m," which could indicate development of a Galaxy Z TriFold 2.

Samsung added a similar "m" tag to the original TriFold during the Z8 series. Beyond that, there's the TriFold 2's availability.

Work on the TriFold has seemingly started late this year, so there's not much to go on. However, it's been alleged that Samsung might keep the TriFold 2 restricted to South Korea and the U.S., like the original model.

item.title: I spent hours tracking down the 12 best Android tablet deals this Black Friday, with prices starting at under $100
item.dc:content:
Black Friday is almost here, and that means savings on all things Android. In my eyes, there's simply no better time to invest in a new Android tablet as there are so many great deals about.

The Best Budget Black Friday Deals For Android Fans

You might be wondering whether you actually need a tablet and, as a frequent Android tablet user myself, I have some advice. If you watch a lot of online content (whether that's YouTube videos or TV series via services like Netflix) they can be a seriously worthwhile purchase as the bigger screens lead to a much more cinematic viewing experience. I find them great to travel with too, as using a tablet for my media needs keeps my phone battery topped up while I'm out and about.

The more powerful, productivity focused models can also work as full-on laptop replacements. I frequently pack a lightweight tablet and keyboard case when I set off for work trips, as it offers a convenient way to draft stories without the hassle of lugging around my heavier (and much more costly to lose) laptop.

If you're thinking about getting in on the Android tablet action, then these are the models I recommend from the ongoing sales.

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Today's best deals — Android Tablets

Tab One: was $139.99 now $99.99
This compact Lenovo tablet is designed for basic day-to-day tasks like responding to emails or browsing the web. It's not particularly powerful, with an older Helio G85 chip, and has just 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage. Still, these are the kind of specs you should expect for under $100 - and you do at least get a free case here.View Deal

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 is a step up from the Lenovo model. It's more powerful, with a more premium aluminum design, though it is still limited by its 64GB storage capacity and 4GB of RAM. There are multiple configurations available, however, and I would recommend paying $30 more for the 128GB version.View Deal

The TCL Tab 10 Gen 4 is a good pick if you want a budget-friendly tablet with a display that's a bit larger and crisper than the Lenovo and Amazon alternatives. The 10.1-inch panel has a 1920×1200 resolution for an improved viewing experience, and it comes with a microSD slot so you can upgrade the 128GB of built-in storage to keep more movies or TV shows downloaded.View Deal

The TCL Tab A1 Plus upgrades the display even further with a 12.2-inch 2.4K resolution panel at a responsive 120Hz refresh rate. The Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 processor and 6GB of RAM also hit the sweet spot between price and performance. This is another model with a microSD card slot, so you can upgrade the 128GB of storage down the line.View Deal

The Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+ doesn't have the greatest specs for its price, with a 90Hz 1920x1200 screen and MediaTek Dimensity 7300 SoC paired with 6GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, but it does offer that beloved Samsung software and is worth it if you want to get into the ecosystem.View Deal

Idea Tab: was $264 now $209.99
I think Lenovo's tablets are seriously underrated. I've tested plenty, and they've always delivered premium build quality and good performance for the price. This MediaTek Dimensity 6300-powered tablet has a 2.5K 90Hz screen and is fitted with 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. It's also bundled with a free case and compatible stlyus pen, making it perfect for students.View Deal

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 offers a larger, higher-resolution 11-inch 2.5K display compared to the Tablet 8. It's got 8GB of RAM and a premium aluminum design. Storage starts at 64GB (on sale for $199.99), but I would seriously recommend buying the 128GB version I've spotlighted here instead, even though it's a little more expensive, so you don't constantly run out of space.View Deal

The NXTPAPER 11 Plus might look like an ordinary tablet, but it actually features TCL's unique NXTPAPER display tech. This lets you transform the screen from a regular tablet display to something that performs more like an e-reader at the press of a button — making this ideal for books and comics. View Deal

Galaxy Tab S10 Lite: was $399.99 now $299.99
Samsung's mid-range Galaxy Tab has received a significant price cut for Black Friday, and it's a strong pick. You're getting a 10.9-inch 90Hz LCD screen, 128GB of storage with the option to expand it with a microSD card, a large 8,000mAh battery, and 6GB of RAM. This bundle includes an S Pen stylus too. View Deal

Galaxy Tab S10 FE: was $549.99 now $349.99
If you can splash out a bit more for the S10 FE, you'll get a higher-resolution display and a faster processor. Other additions, like a fingerprint reader, make for a more convenient user experience. As with the S10 Lite, you're also getting an S Pen stylus here.View Deal

Alexa Tablet 12 Pro: was $499.99 now $399.99
Amazon's most high-end tablet is designed for serious productivity. It's got a speedy 8-core chip, 8GB of RAM, and a 2.8K resolution 120Hz display. This all comes in a sleek aluminum form factor that's lightweight and easy to transportView Deal

Alexa Tablet 12 Pro with Nanomatte display: was $549.99 now $449.99
This upgraded Alexa Tablet 12 Pro comes with Amazon's new Nanomatte display coating, which is designed to cut down glare and make it easy to see what you're doing in even the brightest of environments.View Deal

item.title: Wear it well: The best Black Friday smartwatch and fitness tracker deals from Samsung, Fitbit, and more
item.dc:content:
Smartwatches and fitness trackers are here, there, and everywhere during Black Friday. They're truly inescapable. But at least there are plenty of options to choose from if you're on the hunt for a funky new wearable.

The Best Amazon Echo Black Friday Deals

There couldn't be a better time than Black Friday to really upgrade your fitness game, and now that the new year is just a matter of weeks away, scoring a new wearable just in time for January is the perfect way to ease you back into your fitness regime. And it's even better with a generous price drop.

As the big day gets closer and closer, we're gathering all of the top offers we can find across wearable tech, starting with the best smartwatches. At the moment, our favorite names in wearables, including Samsung, Google, and Garmin (just to list a few), are stacked with price drops on their most popular devices.

Then there are the best fitness trackers, which, if you're looking for something that's more health-oriented, may be the better option for you, especially if you don't want as many distractions or a big bezel that takes up a lot of space on your wrist.

So, what are you waiting for? Your new wearable awaits!

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Charge 6 (Obsidian / Black): was $159.95 now $121.80
The Fitbit Charge 6 has been our overall best fitness tracker since it was released in 2023, combining smartwatch specs with built-in GPS all embedded beneath its stunning AMOLED display. It's not the biggest saving, but its complex roster of health-monitoring tools is worth it, including AFib detection, heart rate variability, breathing rate, and blood oxygen — just to name a few. View Deal

Galaxy Watch 8 [40mm]: was $299.99 now $199.99
The device we described as 'the most comfortable smartwatch' at the time of its release just hit a record-low price this Black Friday. It makes a perfect companion wearable to your Samsung phone, thin and light in design, which, if you want to use it for sleep tracking, shouldn't be a nuisance when wearing it to bed. The only feature we called out was its average battery life, but this shouldn't be a huge issue if you want it for casual use. View Deal

Galaxy Watch Ultra 47mm LTE: was $334.99 now $288
In stark contrast, the Galaxy Watch Ultra is a thick, robust wearable optimized for use in the great outdoors, and its features reflect it too. Its extra LEDs give its tracking accuracy a huge boost, while its 1.5-inch Super AMOLED display offers a clear, bright picture. Battery life is another noticeable upgrade with this model, which, if you plan to use it quite a bit, will certainly come to your advantage. View Deal

5.0 Peak Health and Fitness Tracker with 12-Month Membership: was $239 now $199
Whoop is one of the pioneers behind screenless wearables for a distraction-free, alert-free experience, but it doesn't leave out vital health-tracking metrics, as well as over two weeks' worth of battery life. Though this purchase comes with a 12-month subscription, you'll need to renew it to make the most of the wearable in its entirety, which is the only downside. View Deal

Ring 5: was $399 now $299
Not a fan of smartwatches? Perhaps a smart ring is the way forward for you. Though you'll need the app to check all your metrics, we found that the Oura Ring is a lighter, thinner, and arguably smarter alternative to a smartwatch. It packs detailed, automatic health tracking, an IP68 rating, and red, green, and infrared LEDs — all within the confines of its small build.View Deal

A mere $2 above its lowest-ever price, but one that matches last year's Black Friday listing, so we can't complain. We named the Fitbit Inspire 3 our best value fitness tracker purely for its premium feel and features at a budget-friendly price. This purchase also includes 3 months of Google Health Premium, which includes Gemini-powered adaptive coaching. View Deal

Galaxy Watch 7 [40mm]: was $249.99 now $149
The latest Galaxy Watch 9 isn't currently on sale this Black Friday, but Samsung's previous-gen wearables are just as powerful and more affordable. In this case, the Galaxy Watch 7 packs an upgraded heart rate sensor compared to its predecessor for HR and ECG tracking, serving as a solid option if you're a smartwatch beginner who doesn't want to be locked into a subscription. Last year, the price dropped again around Cyber Monday, so it might be worth holding out for another reduction if you want to take the risk. View Deal

Venu X1 [51mm]: was $799.99 now $499.99
A $300 discount on a 4.5-star smartwatch? Sign me up. The Venu X1 takes the powerful features from the Forerunner 970 and Fenix 8, bringing them together under its unique, bright square display. This is designed for fitness enthusiasts who are serious about their athletic training and want to make the most of premium tools. View Deal

Pixel Watch 5 [45mm]: was $429.99 now $326
Google's latest Pixel Watch just hit a record-low price on Amazon, and though it may not be the most budget-friendly option, over $100 off is undeniably generous. We recommend this over something like the Galaxy Watch 9 purely based on its battery life, which we found lasts roughly two days even with constant sleep and fitness tracking and Gemini use. View Deal

item.title: I trawled the Black Friday sales to track down the best budget Android phone deals with huge savings on Motorola, Samsung, Nothing, and more
item.dc:content:
One of the best things about the Android ecosystem is the number of options available to more cost-conscious buyers, and no time is this more evident than Black Friday. With this year's sale event in full swing this week, we're seeing some incredible discounts on a wide range of phones.

The Best Budget Black Friday Deals For Android Fans

Motorola is currently dominating the budget end of the spectrum in the US, with the prices of some of its most compelling entry-level models slashed. You can find the Motorola Moto G Play on sale for under $100, which is absolutely crazy value. Obviously, a phone this cheap has plenty of limitations (the small amount of RAM and low storage will be sticking points for most users), but the fact that you can find a fully-fledged smartphone for under 100 bucks in 2026 is worth celebrating, and it's a good choice if you have very basic needs or are shopping for a young child or older relative.

The Motorola Moto G Stylus is also an absolute steal at $200 off, too. It's one of the few modern phone models that comes with its own built-in stylus and is very competitive at this price. If you're willing to pay a little more, you can also find discounts on models from TCL, Samsung, and Nothing, so without further ado, let's dive into the best.

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Today's best deals — Phones under $200

Moto G Play: was $149.99 now $99.99
Your options are quite limited if you want a fully fledged smartphone for under $100 this Black Friday, but this model from Motorola is a good choice if you have very basic needs. Expect plenty of limitations given the rock-bottom price, including a modest chipset, 4GB of RAM, just 64GB of storage, and basic cameras. The standout feature is the 90Hz screen, just 720p, but it should feel snappy thanks to the higher-than-usual refresh rate.View Deal

Moto G Power (2025): was $299.99 now $199.99
Another option from Motorola here, with this model focusing on strong battery life and fast charging. It's powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 6300, which is a decent mid-range option, and 8GB of RAM. You also get 128GB of storage. This is a solid deal, but the Moto G Stylus below is a better value pick for the same money, given its higher RRP.View Deal

Includes built-in stylus!

Moto G Stylus (2025): was $399.99 now $199.99
This mid-ranger from Motorola is a bargain at half price and is one of the few affordable options that includes a built-in stylus. It's got 8GB of RAM, a decent chipset, 128GB of storage, and a high-refresh-rate 120Hz display. This would be my personal pick under $200.View Deal

Today's best deals — Phones under $500

Part smartphone and part e-reader, the NXTPAPER 70 Pro boasts a unique 120Hz matte display with an in-built paper mode designed to reduce eye strain when reading. It's perfect for catching up with books or comics on the go, and has decent all-round specs for the price, including 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. Perfect if you want something a little different.View Deal

Galaxy A37 5G (2026): was $489.99 now $389.99
This Samsung mid-ranger is a good alternative if you have more basic usage requirements and don't want to splash out on the higher-spec Galaxy 26 FE (also discounted, as you'll see later on). It's got strong battery life with a 5,000 mAh cell and runs an octa-core SoC that's perfectly capable for daily tasks and light mobile gaming. Samsung also promises security updates until 2032 in some regions - which is a big plus.View Deal

Edge 2026: was $599.99 now $399.99
If you want something more stylish than your usual fare, then Motorola has you covered with its fashion-focused Edge. This phone has a distinct cloth-covered back, which means it feels lovely in the hands. Other highlights include the 5,000mAh battery, triple 50MP camera system, and super bright 5,2000nit 6.3 inch display.View Deal

The Galaxy S26 FE is a great way into the Samsung ecosystem if you don't want to empty your wallet on a high-end phone. It's compact, with a 6.2-inch 120Hz AMOLED display, but still decently powerful thanks to the Exynos 2500 chipset and 8GB of RAM. It's also got strong cameras, with a 50MP main shooter, and comes with 128GB of storage for all your pics.View Deal

New lowest-ever price

Phone (3): was $699 now $499
How much would you pay for Nothing? This stylish smartphone looks like nothing else on the market thanks to a distinct design and an eye-catching Glyph display on the rear, used to show notifications at a glance. The Snapdragon 8s Gen4 chipset delivers solid performance in a wide range of apps and games, and the fact that storage starts at 256GB rather than the usual 128GB is a nice bonus. This is also a new lowest-ever price at Amazon, and it would be my model of choice from this under-$500 lineup.View Deal

item.dc:content:
We're always on the hunt for the latest offers on all things audio, and when it comes to Black Friday sales, I'm all ears.

Whether you're only just getting into the world of audio or you're looking to take your headphone game to the next level, there's something out there for everyone across top dog brands Sony, Bose, and Beats — just to list a few. And I get it, it can be overwhelming trying to cherry-pick deals all by yourself, but that's what we're here for.

Over the next few days, we'll be keeping our eyes peeled for fresh deals and any price drops that come our way, and we'll be updating this hub as we go along — so stay tuned.

We gave the Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro a respectable 4.5 stars, and there's a reason for it. A remarkable upgrade from its predecessors, the audio is even more detailed, with onboard gestures and voice controls, all masked by a fresh redesign. Though you may make the most of its full functionality better with a newer Samsung device, that certainly shouldn't put you off. View Deal

Sony topped its XM5 headphones, which amazed us, by injecting better ANC performance, a battery life that lasts through long work sessions or journeys, and even bringing back the fan-favorite folding ear pads. It's still a little steep even with the price drop, but one we can't complain about for the latest model in the range. View Deal

With 40mm drivers in each ear cup, they offer bold ANC and dynamic head-tracking Spatial Audio, topped with Dolby Atmos support for an even more immersive listening experience. View Deal

Headphone (a): was $199 now $109

item.title: Fitbit Air finally gets this highly requested function — but Google isn’t the one that’s responsible for the rollout
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Cuff is a new Android app that communicates with the Fitbit Air over Bluetooth
  • The app allows you to set custom alerts per app and receive vibration alerts for incoming calls
  • You can also create your own vibration patterns and track food and sleep more smoothly, according to the developer

When Google launched its inaugural screenless fitness tracker, the Fitbit Air, it introduced distraction-free health monitoring to its wearables lineup at a reasonable price — but that also meant sacrificing notifications and important alerts altogether, which, in certain circumstances, can be life-saving.

It's a very simple device, offering limited vibration alerts for alarms, but it lacks support for incoming calls and has very limited customization options, so third-party developers are stepping in.

Sharing the news on Reddit (see below), the minds behind the new Android app Cuff have created a way to give your Fitbit Air the ability to receive alerts for incoming calls via the device's vibration motor. By communicating with your wearable over Bluetooth, the app gives you the freedom to enable alerts for individual apps, create custom vibration patterns, and even receive call alerts from specific people in your contacts list. For iOS users, Airbuzz is a similar alternative.

Sounds handy, doesn't it? But it doesn't draw the line there.

Cuff's personalized alerts are just the start. As detailed in the developer's Reddit post, Cuff supports Stackable Widgets, which let you combine multiple widgets into a single one, eliminating the hassle of creating and relying on separate spaces for each health metric.

But the idea behind the app, the developer says, comes from their longing for an alert feature that's triggered every hour when no movement is detected. Unlike other flagship fitness trackers, this is a small but handy feature left out of the Fitbit Air's roster of capabilities. I have it enabled on my Apple Watch, and it does a solid job of getting me up and moving after sitting at my desk for long intervals.

Food tracking is another tool that Cuff has brought to the Fitbit Air, which the developer says isn't as polished in the Google Health app. There's also a dedicated section that gives you a comprehensive overview of your calorie deficits and surpluses per week, ensuring smoother, more reliable progress-tracking. Additionally, Cuff can track accumulated sleep deficit over a week's period to show you exactly how much sleep you're missing.

When it comes to custom alerts on screenless fitness trackers, I can how some would view the notion as slightly counteractive. If devices like the Fitbit Air are rooted in the goal to eliminate distractions and digital screens, embedding notifications kind of defeats the object.

That said, giving users choices and options is a different matter. Yes, enlisting apps like Cuff opens the notification floodgate, but at least the personalization touch provides some sort of barrier that allows you to draw the line somewhere. For some, incoming calls and other minor alerts, especially from family members, are just as vital as basic health pattern monitoring.

item.title: Rumors say the Galaxy Fit 4 could get pricier—okay, but will its upgrades justify it?
item.dc:content:
Samsung is reportedly gearing up for another fitness tracker after the Galaxy Fit 3 in 2024. Rumors have steadily surfaced, and now we're hearing about its alleged price.

It's a tumultuous time in the tech industry. Prices are soaring all over (even grocery stores are getting hit). A Dealabs (French) rumor about the Galaxy Fit 4 suggests Samsung's next tracker won't dodge a price increase (via SamMobile). The publication reported an alleged price increase for the Fit 4 in Europe. The post states Samsung could raise prices by ~€10 to ~€80 (~$87).

Despite its supposed pricing appearing online, the publication says it's still unclear when Samsung could launch the Fit 4.

This is what we're looking at

No one wants to see prices go up. However, if there is a price increase, is there something under the hood to justify it? Galaxy Fit 4 rumors began in June, suggesting the device would stay true to its fitness-tracker lineage. The device might debut with RTOS (operating system), not Google's Wear OS that you'd find on the Fitbit Air or the Galaxy Watch 9.

As far as what to expect, rumors said the Galaxy Fit 4 would skip Samsung's summer Unpacked (the one we just had). While that was true, reports said Samsung would launch the device a "few months later." We thought September might've been the debut, but it never happened, so we're still waiting. Rumors are still incredibly light on its specifications, which could mean we're still far from a launch.

Right now, all we have to theorize about Samsung's next steps is what the Galaxy Fit 3 featured: a 1.6-inch display, smarter workouts, and a battery that could last up to 13 days. With everything the Galaxy Watch 9 contains, maybe we can expect a few of those health features to slide on over.

Another rumor to mention

Another rumor suggests the Galaxy Fit 4 will lack NFC for contactless payments and a built-in GPS. Instead, consumers might need to rely on their phones for that. It's not a huge dealbreaker, but that added convenience would go a long way. What's more, black, white, and light (icy?) blue colorways were rumored for the Galaxy Fit 4.

We've mentioned this before, but the Galaxy Fit 4's upgrades are a huge curiosity for us. Even more so now that the device could get a price increase.

The Ultrahuman Ring Pro is down to just $299, saving you a massive $180 (38%) from its usual $479 price.

The Ring Pro brings several improvements over the Ring Air, including considerably better battery life and a portable charging case. And unlike Oura's smart rings, you don't need to pay a monthly subscription to access your core health metrics.

✅Recommended if: You want a discreet health tracker with excellent battery life, comprehensive sleep and recovery insights, and no mandatory monthly subscription.

❌Skip this deal if: You primarily want to track workouts in real time, prefer a wearable with a display, or need built-in GPS.

You can simply wear the Ultrahuman Ring Pro throughout the day and let it do its thing in the background. And whenever you want to check your health stats, you can just open the Ultrahuman app on your phone.

Ultrahuman has also improved the heart rate sensor compared to the Ring Air, particularly for tracking sleep and recovery.

But arguably the biggest reason to get the Ultrahuman Ring Pro over other smart rings is its battery life. Ultrahuman claims up to 15 days on a single charge, which means you could potentially go on a two-week vacation without having to charge the ring even once.

What's even better is that, unlike most other smart rings, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro comes with a portable charging case. This means that, similar to a pair of wireless earbuds, you can simply pop the ring into the case to charge it on the go. Ultrahuman claims up to 45 days of combined battery life with the charging case.

The biggest reason, however, to purchase the Ultrahuman Ring Pro over the likes of Oura Ring 5 remains that there's no mandatory subscription to access your everyday health and recovery data. The ring also works with both Android phones and iPhones, so you're not tied to a particular smartphone ecosystem.

At its usual $479 price, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro is admittedly quite expensive for a smart ring. But at $299, especially considering the battery life, included charging case, and lack of a mandatory subscription, it's much easier to recommend.

item.title: Your chaotic Google Messages group chats might finally get threaded replies
item.dc:content:
Google Messages might be getting a much-needed upgrade that could make long conversations much easier to follow.

Google is said to be working on a feature called threaded replies, which will enable users to keep conversations tied to a specific message, rather than having replies scattered around an increasingly chaotic chat, as spotted by the folks at Android Authority. It’s particularly handy for group conversations, where several people can be talking about different things simultaneously, and nobody knows which message they’re actually replying to.

The current setup isn’t really suited for conversations that split into a few smaller ones. Google Messages displays a preview of the original message above each reply, but it can get confusing after a long exchange when unrelated messages begin appearing between responses.

Google’s proposed fix appears to be visually linking related messages. In the chat bubbles, you’ll see a vertical line on the left side that will show which messages are grouped together. A single reply is a straight connecting line; longer exchanges with multiple replies have a small loop in the line. The system works with images and emojis along with text.

Furthermore, Google is also adding reply counters beneath messages in active conversations. That counter can be tapped, and Messages will open a dedicated thread view. The other conversation fades into the background, and you only see the related messages. You have a separate reply box to continue the conversation, as well as an X button to go back to the main conversation.

This should make it much less frustrating to catch up on busy group chats. You can jump right into the conversation that matters, without having to scroll through dozens of unrelated messages to get the context of someone’s reply.

Google is still borrowing from Apple's playbook

The similarities to Apple’s iMessage are difficult to ignore. Apple already has threaded conversations that split out replies from the main chat, and Google seems to be doing something similar. That’s not necessarily a bad thing, though. Messaging apps should strive to make conversations easier to follow, regardless of who first brought an idea up.

For now, threaded replies are an experimental feature hidden in the development code of Google Messages. Google hasn’t announced a release date, and there’s no guarantee the feature will make it to the stable version. But its relatively polished implementation suggests the company is making meaningful strides.

item.title: Razr 2027 leak: earlier launch, and Moto might deliver upgrades that matter
item.dc:content:
Foldables continue to gather steam. Motorola's next wave of 2027 foldables is expected; however, a rumor suggests we might see them earlier.

This morning (Nov. 24), an Android Headlines report alleged what the Motorola Razr 2027 could look like. Rumors suggest upgrades for Moto's 2027 foldable, and it looks like what we were hoping for. The publication alleges the Razr 2027 will finally get rid of the ugly border on its cover display. This has been there since its display was smaller; however, rumors say it could feature a 4-inch cover screen.

A leaked render claims this would expand the Razr 2027's cover display to its hinge, mirroring a Galaxy Z Flip 8 experience or a Razr Ultra. Elsewhere, the leak claims Motorola wants to boost its battery cell. The Razr 2027 could feature a 5,000mAh cell, a 200mAh upgrade from the 2026 variant's 4,800mAh. The foldable's charging might also increase to 45W (up from 30W).

Since these rumors discuss the base Razr model for 2027, Motorola's chip of choice was a hot topic. It seems Motorola will stick with MediaTek's mid-range Dimensity chip line next year. It's not a terrible thing, but given the price of the Razr 2026, which the 2027 version might not be far from, the chosen chip could be better.

Internally, the 8GB of RAM and 256GB of stroage could grace the next Razr. If these rumors sound exciting, they suggest we might not have to wait long. Supposedly, Motorola is gearing up to reveal its Razr 2027 during CES 2027 in early January.

Moto's finally doing work

Android Central's Take

Our wants and desires for the Razr 2027 also mentioned a "mid-range Razr." What we meant was a true mid-range Razr. I agree with this. It'd be nice if all of the Razrs had a stronger, more powerful chip. It kind of sucks having this weaker chip on an otherwise nice foldable phone.

This is a substantial leak, and it's got us thinking back to our original wants and desires for the Razr 2027. The 2026 version wasn't that exciting. It was a decent foldable, yes, but Motorola's "upgrades" weren't all that better. One upgrade we wanted was 256GB of stroage. It's nice to see this rumored, but we need it to actually happen. This year's model cut its storage in half while somehow still increasing its price. It was a distasteful change compared to the 2025 version.

Another area we wanted Motorola to do better in was software upgrades. The 2026 model will only receive three years of OS upgrades and five years of security patches. Unfortunately, according to the publication, that might not change. It sucks when you consider what Google and Samsung are doing: a seven-year promise.

We can't forget to mention Motorola's work with GrapheneOS. This privacy-first software is set to arrive on a selection of Moto phones in 2027. Foldables are on the list, but they will come after. Moreover, you might only see GrapheneOS appear on the Razr Ultra and Fold.

item.title: The Ear Note is Nothing's AI device with a recording case—December launch confirmed
item.dc:content:
AI is everywhere, and now we're getting a closer look at an AI-focused device from Nothing. The company teased it recently, and it might've gone the way you expected.

This week, Mark Gurman from Bloomberg (paywall) sat down with Nothing's CEO, Carl Pei, to discuss what the future holds for its AI device (via GSMArena). First, Gurman teased the device on X, saying the Nothing Ear (Note) is a pair of earbuds "that record and transcribe both in-person meetings and phone calls." Their conversation then shifted to the Ear Note's charging case.

The charging case looks like a proper case (or an old-school cassette recorder). This early glimpse highlighted something familiar: a massive "TALK" button. Pressing "TALK" reportedly lets users record themselves or what's going on around them through the case. While the case is more "external," the earbuds can record phone calls.

Users can also expect transcription. However, this is likely available through the Ear Note companion app. Ear Note will support summaries of previous conversations/recordings, as well as "various AI agents." Carl Pei added more context on X. Pei said, "AI is only as useful as what it knows about you. This is the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI."

The Nothing Ear Note is preparing to launch on December 8. Privacy has been a concern (for users, as well as Nothing), and it was reported that the company integrated safeguards.

Thoughts, questions, concerns?

We should've expected a device with some retro vibes after Carl Pei's teaser earlier this month. Pei gave a small glimpse of Nothing's "screenless AI device." He showed the Ear Note's (as we've come to know it) red and green LED indicators. Pei also said, "context doesn't live in a chat box." The teaser was kept extremely brief ahead of Pei's interview with Bloomberg.

His X post added, "It has no new screen, and it couldn't have been an app." This is interesting because users on social media have likened it to the Essential Recorder app on Nothing phones. It certainly feels similar, but that's because we're trading in one recording app for recording functionality on a pair of earbuds and a case. December 8 will answer everything else we're curious about.

Android Central's Take

I've seen people on social media question why this device exists. I've already called out the Essential Recorder app, as others did on X. Users on Reddit and X also raise privacy concerns. People are curious whether the Ear Note will let them know they're being recorded. Consent is a huge thing, and rightfully so. Personally, I don't necessarily see the need for this. People have joked that this would only be useful for people "constantly hopping between meetings." Even then, I'd rather jot down some quick notes.

item.title: I bought both the Echo Spot and Echo Time smart speakers – and there’s only one I’m keeping on my nightstand this Black Friday
item.dc:content:
As someone who devours live radio and podcasts, there's no smart home item I love more than a bedside smart speaker. I've owned loads of different models over the years, including options from Lenovo, Google, and, of course, Amazon, but my most recent upgrade involved swapping out my reliable Echo Spot in favor of the new Echo Time.

I bought both speakers for full price on their respective launch days, and have had plenty of time to test the two models and really get to grips with the many differences between them. Whether you should go with the Echo Spot or Echo Time is likely going to be a big question this Black Friday. After all, the Echo Spot has dropped to just $44.99 (down from $109.99) as part of the sale, while the Echo Time has fallen to $99.99 (from $199.99) thanks to a mega 50% off discount.

But is the Echo Time actually worth double the cost? Here's everything you need to know about the two models, and my take on which is the better pick in the ongoing sales.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

The Amazon Echo Spot is the better pick if you want a basic, distraction-free listening experience. It features a small screen that's used for little more than displaying a clock face and showing some simple animations. Of course, as an Alexa speaker, you can also ask it for the weather, to tell fun jokes, or set alarms.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You want a simple, no-nonsense smart speaker for your nightstand. The Echo Spot has a compact display that is used to show you the time and, occasionally, a basic animation or two. It's the ideal model if you want something that functions like a standard clock, but with the added smart-speaker functionality of Alexa.

❌Skip this deal if: You're after a more advanced, customizable bedside companion with better sound. I frequently found myself frustrated by the limitations of the Echo Spot, particularly the limited number of very basic clock faces that you can choose from. The Echo Time blows it away in terms of customizability. The Time also sounds better, with more detailed and rich audio.

Better sound and more customization

The newer Echo Time offers richer and more detailed sound than the Spot. It's also much more customizable, with a wide range of clock face options that you can tweak to your liking. The larger screen dims at night, so it doesn't keep you awake, and gently illuminates in the morning to help you wake up. In my eyes, all of this is well worth the extra $55 if you have the budget.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You want an all-round, more advanced bedside companion. While the Echo Spot was released back in 2024, the Echo Time came out earlier this year – and you can really tell, given just how much more advanced it is than its predecessor. It boasts a large, round display that you can customize with a wide range of clock faces, as well as noticeably upgraded sound that's both richer and more detailed.

I also think the design looks and feels much more premium in your home. The Echo Spot has a matte plastic finish and a basic cloth cover over its speaker grille, while the Echo Spot is covered with this lovely woven material all over.

❌Skip this deal if: You think the Echo Spot will meet your needs. If you are simply after a small screen that can display the time and decent, but not exceptional, sound, you will most likely still be able to make do with the more basic Spot – and save yourself some cash in the process.

item.title: I compared the heavily discounted Echo Dot Max and 5th Gen Echo Dot to find out which is the best deal this Black Friday
item.dc:content:
Amazon has won the smart home Olympics with its range of Echo devices, but it's tricky to settle on one when there are so many options out there — and the Black Friday madness doesn't help, either.

There are two star devices in Amazon's Black Friday event: the 5th-gen Echo Dot and the newer Echo Dot Max, both of which are some of the best smart speakers out there. On a regular day, you'd be paying the best part of $100 for each, but the current Black Friday offers are hard to ignore.

As for the previous-gen model, the Echo Dot is now $39.99 down from $79.99, while the upgraded Echo Dot Max is $49.99 down from $199.99. So what's the difference between the two devices, and how do you decide which one is best for you?

Similarities-wise, both are compact smart speakers that any bookcase, media unit, or countertop can adorn. Both support Amazon's upgraded AI voice assistant, Alexa+, and both speakers have fine-tuned inner workings that boost mighty audio performance - but the Echo Dot Max's upgrades could be the reason you spend a little more.

Though the 5th-gen Echo Dot is far from a poor smart hub, its newer sibling is more advanced not only on the audio side, but also on the smart home front, which you can dive into below. For those who aren't too fussed with getting all the bells and whistles, the Echo Dot is plenty to get you by, but for just $10 extra you'll be getting a lot more — I know which one I'd be spending my money on this Black Friday.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Echo Dot (5th-Gen): was $79.99 now $39.99
It's not the lowest price we've seen for this Echo device, but who can say no to a $40 smart speaker? It's compact, fits nicely in any room, and doesn't fall flat on offering a bold audio experience. Despite being a previous gen model, it's a top pick for us, and one we always keep an eye out for during Black Friday. View Deal

✅Recommended if: You're not the biggest audiophile and want a device that can fill a room with punchy sound at an affordable price. If you're interested in taking advantage of Alexa+ smarts but don't feel up for upgrading to the latest models, the 5th-gen Echo Dot supports this, but newer models may get updates a lot sooner.

❌Skip this deal if: You want a device that has more than just Matter support. If you have other smart home devices running on Thread or Zigbee, the 5th-gen Echo Dot won't be able to tie them together due to the lack of support. If you have the extra money to spend on the Echo Dot Max, you might as well cash in and make the most of its upgraded capabilities.

Echo Dot Max: was $199.99 now $49.99
One of Amazon's newest smart speakers on the scene is less than $50, and it's a beast. With a two-way speaker system, its audio performance is a significant upgrade compared to its predecessor and is one of the first flagship Alexa+ speakers — meaning it comes with the AI-powered assistant's smarts out of the box. View Deal

✅Recommended if: You've been using a previous-gen smart speaker for a few years and want a bit of an audio boost. Compared to the 5th-gen Echo Dot, it delivers three times the bass, which can be credited to its revamped audio smarts — packing a two-way system with a dedicated subwoofer and tweeter.

If your old smart home hub is giving you nothing but laggy responses, this is your next reason to upgrade. The Echo Dot Max is powered by the AZ3 chip to help Alexa respond to your requests with more speed and accuracy, as well as better wake-word detection and on-device processing for AI tasks.

It's also Matter, Thread, and Zigbee compatible, so if you have other devices dotted around in your setup, the Echo Dot Max can fit in smoothly as a new central hub.

❌Skip this deal if: You're satisfied with the current audio performance and responsiveness of your current smart speaker. The Echo Dot Max is recommended for those who can tell the difference in audio quality and want the upgrade; if this isn't a huge concern for you and you need a device that just gets the job done, previous-gen models are still solid alternatives.

item.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra leak reveals Samsung is stripping away another camera feature
item.dc:content:
Samsung might be gearing up for another big change to its flagship phone cameras. A new leak suggests Samsung is likely to ditch the laser autofocus hardware, possibly taking the 3x telephoto camera with it. That’s two changes to the rear camera system, and while neither is necessarily a recipe for photographic trouble, it does bring up an interesting question: what does Samsung intend to use instead?

The claim comes from well-known leaker Ice Universe, who shared the alleged changes on X. Samsung has been using laser autofocus in its Ultra phones since the Galaxy S21 Ultra, so this is a departure from a camera setup the company has used for several generations.

For the uninitiated, the laser autofocus module is supposed to emit an infrared beam and calculate the time it takes to bounce back from a subject, then use the distance information to assist the camera in locking focus.

This is particularly helpful in low-light situations, where traditional phase-detection autofocus (PDAF) can struggle. But laser autofocus has its own limitations. It struggles with distant subjects, bright sunlight and moving objects.

That doesn't necessarily mean the S27 Ultra will have a worse camera. Autofocus technology has come a long way. Both dual-pixel and all-pixel autofocus can calculate the distance to a subject by using multiple light-sensitive areas across the image sensor. This technology is already being used in some of Samsung’s other flagship devices, so the ditching of a separate laser module is not necessarily a step backward.

A bigger camera overhaul could be coming

It’s also rumored that Samsung might utilize its new 200MP ISOCELL HP6 sensor for the Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro. Previous reports have indicated support for LOFIC, a technology that’s designed to improve HDR photography and preserve detail in the brightest and darkest parts of a photo. It’s not known if the new sensor will also introduce an advanced autofocus system as well.

The bigger question is what these hardware changes portend for everyday photography. The lack of a dedicated 3x camera may mean more reliance on cropping the sensor for zoom ranges in between. The removal of laser autofocus may mean more reliance on the main sensor’s focusing system.

None of these changes have been confirmed by Samsung, and we won’t see the Galaxy S27 family until the first quarter of 2027. Whether these rumored changes are a smart play for newer imaging tech or just another instance of stripping out useful hardware to cut costs is something buyers will want answered before splashing out flagship money.

item.dc:content:
Working on something cool in the mobile space? Submit it to the Android Central CES 2027 Awards!

Intended to represent the very best of technology at CES 2027, we're seeking award entries that demonstrate outstanding innovation and industry excellence across a wide range of technology categories, particularly mobile.

Android Central CES 2027 Awards categories

We will be picking our favorites in the following categories.

  • Best of Show
  • Best Premium Android Phone
  • Best Budget Android Phone
  • Best Android Tablet
  • Best Mobile Accessory
  • Best Wearable
  • Most Innovative Design
  • Most Exciting Software Innovation
  • The "I Can't Believe It's Real Award" (Spotlighting the most exciting concept product)

Please note that the categories are subject to change based on what we see at the show. Entries for all categories will be reviewed and judged by our team.

How to enter a product for consideration for an Android Central CES Award

Submissions must be received by noon EST / 9 a.m. PST on Dec. 10, 2026. Winners will be announced during the show.

To submit a product for consideration, please fill out the Android Central CES Awards submission form.

To be eligible, products must be new (or have been materially updated since CES 2026) and have a presence at CES 2027.

We are happy to sign and keep embargoes on unannounced products if you wish for them to be considered. If you have any questions, please email editors@androidcentral.com.

In addition to online submissions, we will be exploring the show floor, seeking new and interesting products to add to our list of nominees.
